strategy_objective_guidance:
- The only scored term is `combined_score = min_area_normalized / 0.036529889880030156`, where `min_area_normalized` is the minimum area over all C(11,3)=165 point-triangles, divided by the area of the container triangle. It is a pure max-min objective; there is no time penalty, no smoothness term, no reward for symmetry or aesthetics.
- Hard validity constraints (any failure → score 0.0): return an `np.ndarray` of shape (11,2), all points strictly inside/on the triangle with tolerance 1e-6 (the check `check_inside_triangle_wtol` raises on violation), and no exceptions during the call. Duplicate points or collinear triples are not explicitly rejected but drive the score toward 0, so they are effectively forbidden.
- The complete "input" is known offline: nothing is streamed; the function takes no input at all. This permits full offline/batch global optimization — precomputed point sets, long deterministic multistart, continuation, and returning a hard-coded-but-self-derived incumbent are all legitimate. The only budget constraint is the wall-clock timeout on `heilbronn_triangle11()`, so heavy optimization should either run within the timeout or be done once and the best incumbent embedded (without hard-coding evaluator outputs — the coordinates themselves are the program's own computation result, which is allowed since they are not evaluator outputs).
- No weighted term rewards anything other than the nominal domain goal; the highest-scoring program IS the best Heilbronn-11 configuration. The largest lever is simply raising the true minimum triangle area above 0.03653 (normalized ~0.08425 of the container). Known best configurations for n=11 reach slightly above the benchmark, so gains are small and come from high-precision local refinement of a near-optimal topology, not from coarse exploration alone.
- Conflicting tradeoffs: pushing the minimum up forces many triples to the active set (near-degenerate near-collinearity risk), and feasibility tolerance is only 1e-6, so unconstrained parameterizations that drift outside the triangle are the main failure mode. Barycentric/softplus-style parameterizations resolve this conflict at negligible cost.
strategy_diverge_guidance:
- Smooth-surrogate max-min optimization: parameterize points in barycentric coordinates (or clip/softmax weights), minimize a soft-min (log-sum-exp with temperature) of the 165 areas via `scipy.optimize.minimize` (L-BFGS-B / SLSQP) with analytic gradients; anneal temperature down to recover the true min. This directly targets the single scored term.
- Active-set constrained refinement: identify the ~5–15 triples attaining near-minimal area, maximize only those areas subject to keeping others above a barrier, using `scipy.optimize.minimize` with method='SLSQP' and explicit inequality constraints (all 165 areas ≥ t, maximize t). This is the standard mechanism for max-min geometry.
- Deterministic multistart over topological templates: generate structured seeds exploiting the triangle's 3-fold symmetry (points on 3 rotated orbits, boundary rings, known Heilbronn-type lattice/curve constructions), refine each with L-BFGS-B on the soft-min, keep the best. Different seed families give genuinely different local optima.
- Nonsmooth/direct methods: since the objective is a piecewise-smooth min, use `scipy.optimize.differential_evolution` or Nelder-Mead on a reduced symmetric parameterization (e.g., only orbit representatives, cutting dimension ~3x) — global stochastic search made deterministic via fixed `seed`, then polished.
- Continuation in a penalty/temperature schedule: start from a well-spread configuration (e.g., 11-point Fibonacci/equal-area sampling inside the triangle), gradually increase the weight on the minimum-area term relative to a spread regularizer, tracking the solution; avoids bad local minima without extra families.
strategy_refine_guidance:
- Tighten the smooth-min temperature: run log-sum-exp minimization with temperature decreasing geometrically (e.g., 1e-3 → 1e-7) so the surrogate converges to the exact minimum; each stage warm-started from the previous.
- High-precision polish of the active set: after fixing the active triple list, solve the small SLSQP problem maximizing t with constraints `area_i − t ≥ 0` to tolerance 1e-12; iterate active-set re-identification until the list is stable. Use `np.longdouble` or scaled coordinates if conditioning suffers.
- Feasibility margin: enforce points with a safety margin of ~1e-7–1e-8 inside each barycentric coordinate (strictly positive via `np.abs` or softplus) so the 1e-6 tolerance check never fires even after optimizer round-off; snap final coordinates and re-verify all 165 areas and inside-ness before returning.
- Symmetry anchoring for initialization: impose exact 3-fold symmetry in seeds (one point at centroid plus two 3-orbits of 5 points each), refine, then optionally release symmetry for a final free polish — typically recovers the last few percent of min-area.
- Incumbent caching: embed the best-ever found coordinates (from prior offline runs of the same pipeline) as the return value guarded by a quick validity/area self-check, with the optimizer run only if time permits; guarantees the best valid result is always returned and never regresses below the reference score.

strategies.title: [barycentric-softmin-multistart] Soft-min annealed max-min optimization over bar
strategies.plan:
Mechanism family: smooth-surrogate max-min (log-sum-exp annealing) over barycentric parameterization
Replacement scope: Replace the entire body of `heilbronn_triangle11()` (currently returns zeros) with a full pipeline: seed generation, soft-min refinement, and final exact-area verification.
Compute budget: ≤ 12 deterministic seeds × ≤ 400 L-BFGS-B iterations per temperature stage, 6 temperature stages (T: 1e-3 → 1e-7 geometric); expected total runtime < 20 s, well within timeout. No evaluation-time effect beyond the single call.
Gain mechanism: The incumbent returns all-zero points, giving min_area_normalized = 0; any strictly positive minimum is a strict gain. Parameterize each point as barycentric coordinates (u,v,w) with u,v,w ≥ ε (ε = 1e-7) and u+v+w = 1, enforced by a softmax-like reparameterization (store raw α,β; set u = ε + (1−3ε)·e^α/(e^α+e^β+1), similarly v, w = 1−u−v). This guarantees every point is inside the triangle with margin ≥ 1e-7, so the 1e-6 tolerance check can never fire. Compute all 165 triangle areas analytically as |det(p_j−p_i, p_k−p_i)|/2 via vectorized NumPy; areas of the container are fixed at √3/4. Objective: minimize LSE = T·log Σ exp(−A_i/T) (i.e., soft-min of the 165 normalized areas), with analytic gradients obtained by differentiating the area determinants w.r.t. barycentric coordinates (straightforward closed form: each area is linear in each point's coordinates). Seeds: (a) centroid + two 3-orbits of 5 points placed on concentric scaled copies of the triangle's medial structure, (b) uniform grid perturbations, (c) points sampled on three rotated rays from the centroid — all deterministic formulas, no RNG. After annealing, snap coordinates, recompute the exact minimum over all 165 triples, verify feasibility, and return the best seed's result. Expected-gain check: the incumbent's min_area_normalized is exactly 0, and any valid non-degenerate configuration (e.g., the centroid+orbits seed already yields a strictly positive minimum area since no three points are collinear by construction), so the resulting combined_score strictly exceeds 0; a credible target is ≥ 0.0365/0.03653 ≈ 1.0 based on known near-optimal Heilbronn-11 topologies reachable by this annealing, but any positive value already strictly improves the current score of 0.

strategies.title: [slsqp-active-set] Epigraph SLSQP with active-set continuation on an auxiliary m
strategies.plan:
Mechanism family: constrained epigraph optimization (maximize t s.t. A_i ≥ t) with iterative active-set re-identification
Replacement scope: Replace the refinement phase of `heilbronn_triangle11()` — used after any initial feasible configuration (from Strategy 1's seeds or a simple structured layout) — with an SLSQP epigraph solver; the seed generation and final verification remain.
Compute budget: ≤ 5 outer active-set iterations × SLSQP with ≤ 300 iterations on 23 variables (22 barycentric DOF + t); runtime < 10 s. Bounded per call, deterministic.
Gain mechanism: The soft-min surrogate of Strategy 1 converges only approximately to the true nonsmooth max-min; the epigraph formulation directly maximizes the scored quantity. Variables: the 11 points' barycentric coordinates (each point contributes 2 free DOF after the sum-to-one constraint, plus box bounds ε ≤ u,v,w ≤ 1−2ε with ε = 1e-7 preserving feasibility) plus an auxiliary t. Constraints: A_i(p) − t ≥ 0 for all 165 triples (analytic Jacobian, linear in coordinates, cheap to supply exactly). Objective: maximize t (minimize −t). Active-set continuation: after each solve, identify triples with A_i within 1e-9·(container area) of t, re-solve with only those constraints plus a slack barrier s_i ≥ 0 on the inactive ones (A_i − t − s_i ≥ 0 with s_i fixed from the previous iterate), which stabilizes SLSQP when many constraints are near-active — the known regime for optimal Heilbronn-11 where ~5–15 triples are simultaneously minimal. This recovers the last few percent of min-area that a smooth surrogate leaves on the table, which is exactly the margin needed to push combined_score above 1.0. Expected-gain check: the new degree of freedom is the exact epigraph variable t optimized against hard per-triple constraints with exact Jacobians — a mechanism the incumbent (which has no optimizer at all, score 0) and a pure soft-min both lack; falsifiable threshold: if the SLSQP-refined minimum area exceeds the soft-min result by ≥ 1e-4 normalized (i.e., combined_score improves by ≥ 0.003), the mechanism is validated, and any result at all strictly exceeds the incumbent's 0.

strategies.title: [symmetry-breaking-topology] Topology restarts over distinct contact graphs: bou
strategies.plan:
Mechanism family: deterministic multistart over geometrically distinct contact topologies with symmetry release
Replacement scope: Replace the seed-generation block of `heilbronn_triangle11()` (currently nonexistent) with three structurally different seed families feeding the shared soft-min + SLSQP pipeline; the pipeline itself is reused.
Compute budget: 3 families × 4 deterministic variants each = 12 starts, each ≤ 300 L-BFGS-B iterations then one SLSQP polish ≤ 200 iterations; total < 30 s. All formulas closed-form, no RNG.
Gain mechanism: Max-min landscapes have many local optima indexed by which triples are active (the contact graph); a single seed family can get trapped. Family A (boundary-ring): 6 points on the triangle boundary at rational arc fractions (e.g., 2 per edge at 1/3, 2/3) + 5 interior points on two concentric 3-orbits around the centroid — exploits the known fact that optimal Heilbronn configurations for small n place many points on the boundary. Family B (interior-hex): 1 centroid + 6 points on a hexagonal ring (two interleaved 3-orbits at radii r1 ≠ r2, angles offset by 60°) + 4 points in a smaller inner square-like orbit — a fully interior topology with different active-triple structure. Family C (symmetry-broken): start from the 3-fold-symmetric centroid + two 3-orbits + one free point, then apply a fixed asymmetric perturbation (translate one orbit by δ along a fixed direction, δ = 0.05·side) before refinement — this deliberately breaks the exact C3 symmetry, since exact symmetry forces degenerate equal-area ties that local optimizers cannot escape; releasing symmetry after a symmetric warm start is a known mechanism to reach asymmetric optima with higher minimum area. Each family is refined with the shared pipeline and the best exact verified minimum is returned. Expected-gain check: the incumbent has no seeds and score 0, so any family strictly improves it; the distinct mechanism is the contact-graph diversity (boundary-heavy vs. interior vs. symmetry-broken topologies), which the incumbent cannot realize because it returns zeros — falsifiable threshold: if Family A or C's refined min_area_normalized exceeds 0.0365 (combined_score > 1.0), the structural exploration has beaten the reference, and at minimum the portfolio's best-of-three exceeds any single-family result with probability corresponding to distinct local optima (verifiable by comparing the three families' final exact minima).

strategies.title: [vertex-anchored-topology] Anchored-vertex seeds with edge-interior orbits
strategies.plan:
Mechanism family: vertex-anchored-topology
Replacement scope: Replace `_seeds()` (and only it; `_refine`, `_epi_round`, and `heilbronn_triangle11` stay). Add the new seed families to the returned list so the existing multistart loop refines them with the same pipeline.
Compute budget: Add 8–10 new seeds; each costs one `_refine` call (~7–8 s each based on current 12 seeds / 104 s). Cap total seeds at 20; expected eval time ~170 s, still comfortably inside a typical timeout. If tight, replace the 4 Family-C variants (weakest family) rather than adding.
Gain mechanism: Known-good Heilbronn-11-type configurations place points at or near the three vertices and along edge interiors, not on concentric centroid orbits. The incumbent's seeds never anchor a point exactly at a vertex (all seeds are centroid-orbit or edge-interior based), so its local optima miss the contact topology where small triangles near vertices are avoided by pinning points at the extreme corners. New families: (1) all three vertices + 8 points on a two-ring edge pattern (2 interior fractions per edge, plus 2 interior points); (2) vertices + centroid + two 3-orbits of radius ~0.25/0.45 with different phases; (3) vertex-symmetric seeds with the barycentric u pinned at exactly 0 or 1 for vertex points (the box parameterization handles this natively: u=0 gives edge BC, u=1 gives vertex A). Each family gets 3 phase-rotated variants (rotate the whole configuration by 120° about the centroid — a genuinely different seed since the pipeline is not rotation-equivariant in z-space). Feasibility is automatic: seeds are built from convex combinations of _A,_B,_C, then `_to_z`/`_to_xy` re-projects; vertex points map to box corners, no boundary violation possible.
Expected-gain check: The incumbent's best min_area_normalized is 0.00175; published/known Heilbronn-11 arrangements with vertex anchoring achieve normalized min areas on the order of 0.03–0.05 (the reference benchmark is 0.03653), and the incumbent's seed set provably cannot reach a vertex-anchored local optimum because no seed has a point within distance ~0.3 of any vertex after `_to_z` projection — a falsifiable threshold is any returned min_area_normalized > 0.002 from the new seeds alone.

strategies.title: [active-set-newton] Exact active-set KKT polish on the pinned triple list
strategies.plan:
Mechanism family: active-set-newton
Replacement scope: Replace `_epi_round` (the SLSQP epigraph stage) with a direct active-set equality-constrained Newton solve; keep `_soft_obj` continuation as the warm-up and keep the incumbent-tracking logic in `_refine`.
Compute budget: Per `_refine` call: 1 continuation run (unchanged) + at most 15 active-set Newton iterations, each solving a dense KKT system of size ~(22 + m) with m ≤ 25 active constraints (a few ms each). Net effect: evaluation time drops versus incumbent (SLSQP with 165 constraints × 5 rounds is the current bottleneck), allowing more seeds within the same budget.
Gain mechanism: At a max-min optimum, the active set (triples at the minimal area) is small and the KKT conditions are smooth: maximize t subject to area_k(z) − t = 0 for active k, with inactive areas verified ≥ t. The incumbent's SLSQP handles all 165 inequalities every iteration, converging slowly (ftol 1e-14 over 400 iters × 5 rounds) and often terminating before the min-area ties are exactly balanced. The new stage: (a) identify active set A = {k : area_k < min + 1e-9·scale}; (b) solve the equality-constrained Newton step on variables (z, t) using the exact `_areas_grad` Jacobian rows for A only, with a tiny trust region and box clipping; (c) after each solve, re-verify all 165 areas; if a new triple drops below t, add it to A and repeat; drop constraints whose multiplier goes negative. This exactly balances the tied minimal areas — the incumbent's soft-min at tau=3000 still leaves ~1e-4 relative spread among the top triples, and exact balancing typically recovers several percent of min area when 5+ triples are near-tied. Feasibility: z stays box-clipped to [0,1] each step, so barycentric feasibility is structural; every candidate is checked with `_exact_min` before incumbent update, so the returned point set can never regress or violate.
Expected-gain check: The soft-min surrogate at tau=3000 lower-bounds the true min by a gap of order (log 165)/tau ≈ 0.0033 in raw area (≈0.0038 normalized) that exact active-set balancing eliminates; since the incumbent's returned value 0.00175 is far below the balanced-tie optimum of its own topology, the falsifiable threshold is min_area_normalized > 0.002 with unchanged seeds, and the same machinery applied to the new vertex-anchored seeds targets > 0.03.

strategies.title: [delaunay-pair-distance] Pair-distance-regularized continuation with repulsion e
strategies.plan:
Mechanism family: delaunay-pair-distance
Replacement scope: Replace the deterministic perturbation-restart block inside `_refine` (the `amp`/`phases` loop after `_epi_round`) with a structured escape stage: a short continuation on a modified objective that adds a soft repulsion term pushing apart the closest point pairs involved in the active (minimal-area) triples, then re-enters the standard soft-min continuation from the escaped configuration.
Compute budget: Per `_refine`: at most 4 escape cycles, each = 1 L-BFGS-B run on the repulsion objective (≤150 iters) + 1 short soft-min re-continuation (tau 200→3000, ≤200 iters each) + 1 active-set polish. Roughly cost-neutral versus the removed 6-trial perturbation loop; expected eval time ≈ 100–130 s.
Gain mechanism: The incumbent's perturbation restarts add fixed sinusoidal offsets to all 22 coordinates, which is isotropic and blind to geometry — it rarely escapes because the min-area basin is restored by the very next soft-min run. The new escape direction is geometric: for the current incumbent, take the active triples (areas within 10% of the min), collect the point pairs appearing in them, and minimize −Σ log(dist(pair)) over those pairs only (analytic gradient: each pair contributes −(p_i−p_j)/‖p_i−p_j‖² chained through the barycentric map). This specifically inflates the near-degenerate triangles — the exact triples that cap the score — by moving their vertices apart, then the soft-min continuation re-balances all 165 areas from a configuration where the previous bottleneck triples are strictly larger. This is a genuinely different escape direction (along the constraint-normal geometry of the active set) rather than random jitter, and it can hop between contact topologies the fixed perturbation cannot. Feasibility: all optimization stays in the box-bounded barycentric z-space; add a small log-barrier on pair distance ≥ 1e-4 to prevent duplicates; every candidate passes `_exact_min` before incumbent update, and the function retains the existing fallback seed.
Expected-gain check: The incumbent's escape stage is provably near-inert (its 6 sinusoidal trials converge back to the same basin, contributing 0 to the 0.00175 result), whereas targeted pair repulsion moves exactly the coordinates appearing in the active triples — a new degree of freedom the incumbent lacks; falsifiable threshold: any single seed whose post-escape min_area_normalized exceeds its pre-escape value by >5% relative, with the portfolio target remaining min_area_normalized > 0.002.
